messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find the angle of the force for a given momentum. Likely they have momentum vector and want to find angle of force? But force is derivative of momentum: F = dp/dt. If momentum is known as a vector, the force direction is the direction of change of momentum. If momentum is constant, force zero. If momentum changes, the force direction is along the change vector. So angle of force relative to something? Might need to compute angle of vector using arctan2. Use function calculate_vector_angle. Provide explanation. Use degrees or radians. Provide example. Also mention that if momentum vector is given, you can compute its angle relative to x-axis. But force is derivative. So if momentum is changing, the force direction is along the change vector. So angle of force = angle of dp/dt vector. So if we have momentum components p_x, p_y, and their rates of change dp_x/dt, dp_y/dt, then angle = atan2(dp_y/dt, dp_x/dt). Provide code. Use function.
